introduction.summary: In a fluidized bed reactor, gas blown up through a distributor plate lifts a bed of fine particles so they behave like a boiling liquid. video_tutorials.title: Fluidized Bed Reactor — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Fluidized Bed Reactor.
In a fluidized bed reactor gas blown up through a distributor lifts fine solid particles so the bed behaves like a boiling liquid.
Excellent mixing gives uniform temperature; internal cyclones recover entrained particles and return them to the bed.
Typical applications include fluid catalytic cracking (FCC); polyethylene/polypropylene gas-phase reactors; roasting and calcination; biomass gasification.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Fluidized Bed Reactor — Operation

script.narration: How the Fluidized Bed Reactor works.
Fluidizing gas enters the plenum below the distributor.
Gas through the caps lifts the particles — the bed expands and bubbles.
Bubbles rise and burst at the surface.
Cyclones separate entrained particles and return them through diplegs.
Product gas leaves at the top.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Fluidized Bed Reactor — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Fluidized Bed Reactor.
Monitor bed ΔP and temperatures.
Inspect distributor nozzles and cyclones.
Refractory and erosion repairs.
Watch for defluidization / agglomeration: δp change, hot spots. Common cause: sticky particles, low gas flow.
Watch for cyclone erosion: catalyst losses. Common cause: high velocity.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
